title: Columbia Bank’s 8th Annual Week of Giving Donates More Than 2,200 Volunteer Hours to New Jersey and New York Nonprofits
summary: Columbia Bank is proud to announce the successful completion of its 8th annual Week of Giving, an employee-driven initiative dedicated to supporting communities across New Jersey and New York. In the two weeks leading up to Thanksgiving, Team Columbia contributed more than 2,265 hours of service, supporting over 63 organizations across New Jersey and New York.
body_markdown:
Columbia Bank is proud to announce the successful completion of its 8th annual Week of Giving, an employee-driven initiative dedicated to supporting communities across New Jersey and New York. In the two weeks leading up to Thanksgiving, Team Columbia contributed more than 2,265 hours of service, supporting over 63 organizations across New Jersey and New York. This year marks the first time Week of Giving has supported the New York region, made possible by Columbia Bank’s recent merger with Northfield Bank. The initiative reflects Columbia Bank’s commitment to giving back by encouraging nearly 100% employee participation in volunteer activities during company time.


“Our Week of Giving continues to grow in both reach and impact, and this year’s expansion into New York for the first time, following our merger with Northfield Bank, is a milestone for Team Columbia. Extending our reach to Staten Island and Brooklyn allows us to bring our employees together to support organizations serving communities throughout New Jersey and New York,” said Thomas J. Kemly, President and CEO of Columbia Bank. “This expansion reflects our commitment to being a true partner in every community we serve. We’re grateful for the opportunity to give back, build meaningful connections, and support the important work these organizations do every day.”


This year’s volunteer efforts expanded across communities throughout New Jersey and New York; reaching 13 New Jersey counties as well as Staten Island and Brooklyn. Volunteers made a meaningful impact in their communities through a variety of hands-on projects, including preparing and serving meals, collecting winter clothing, assembling hygiene and school-supply kits, and packing Thanksgiving meals. They also brought some holiday cheer by decorating community facilities, painting homes and recreation centers, and supporting winter craft activities for children, seniors, and adults with disabilities. Strategically positioned before Thanksgiving, Columbia Bank strengthened efforts through donating 135 turkeys to families in need.
